title: Backfill event v2 without breaking mixed-version readers
prompt:
Repair `migration.go`, the bounded v1-to-v2 event backfill. Keep the existing public API. Each `RunBatch` call may process at most one store batch. Load its durable checkpoint first and return without further store work when it is complete. Pass the checkpoint token to `ListBatch` unchanged with exactly the configured batch size, reject an oversized response before processing it, and handle events in the order returned by storage. Resume tokens are opaque: persist `Batch.NextToken` byte-for-byte and use `Batch.Complete` as the only end-of-scan signal, including when a final token is non-empty.

A v1 JSON payload has required non-empty string fields `type` and `timestamp`. Its v2 representation is additive: set reserved fields `event_type` and `occurred_at` from those legacy fields while retaining `type`, `timestamp`, and every unrelated JSON field. Do not round unknown numbers through `float64`, and do not mutate the supplied payload buffer. Existing reserved v2 fields in a v1 record are stale and must be replaced from the legacy fields. A listed v2 event is already current and must never be rewritten, so old and new publishers can coexist throughout the rollout. Unsupported versions and malformed v1 payloads must fail the batch without checkpoint advancement.

Rewrite a v1 event with its optimistic `Revision` and a deterministic non-empty operation ID scoped to the migration ID and immutable event ID. The operation ID must not depend on revision, page position, or retry count, and must remain identical across every attempt for that event. A successful idempotent replay (`RewriteResult.Applied == false`) still completes the logical rewrite. Only errors matching `ErrTransient` are write-retryable; `maxWriteRetries` is the number of retries after the initial attempt. Because a transient response may arrive after commit, retry with the same operation ID and precondition so the store can guarantee exactly one physical rewrite.

On `ErrVersionConflict`, count the conflict, re-read the event, and use the latest state. If it is now v2, accept the coexisting writer's value without overwriting it. If it remains v1, recompute the additive payload from that latest record and retry with the same operation ID and new revision. `maxConflictRetries` is also the number of retries after the initial attempt. Other rewrite and reload errors are not retryable.

Save the page checkpoint only after every event in the returned batch has completed. A checkpoint save can commit and still return any error, so after a save error re-load the checkpoint and accept success only when its token and completion flag exactly match the attempted state. Otherwise return the original save error and do not overwrite the durable state.

Keep `Stats` exact: `Scanned` once per returned event; `Rewritten` once for each logical rewrite completed by this call; `AlreadyV2` for each listed or conflict-reloaded event accepted as v2; `Conflicts` for every observed version conflict; `WriteRetries` for transient retries actually made; and `Batches` only after the checkpoint is known durable. On failure, return partial stats and contextual errors that preserve identity through `errors.Is`.

Do not modify `model.go`, `fake_store.go`, `go.mod`, `protected_tests/`, or `tests/`. Verification is local, offline, and deterministic. Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py` from the repository root.

full_distill.primary_skill: implement a bounded resumable Go event-schema backfill with additive JSON preservation, optimistic conflict recovery, and idempotent exactly-once rewrites
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the current migrator lists from the beginning after every restart, sorts events out of storage order, checkpoints before rewriting, guesses completion from token spelling, drops legacy and unknown JSON fields, and has no transient-write or version-conflict recovery
full_distill.success_contract: each invocation processes no more than one bounded page in storage order, preserves opaque continuation state and every compatible payload field, leaves existing or concurrently published v2 events untouched, retries ambiguous writes with one stable operation ID, and advances a checkpoint only after the complete page is known durable
adversarial_factors: non-semantic non-empty final cursors distinguish the explicit completion flag from cursor guessing, while a second invocation must pass a saved cursor back unchanged
storage order deliberately disagrees with event-ID order and the first page mixes v1 and v2 records, exposing sorting and unconditional rewrite implementations
unknown nested values, a beyond-float64 integer, legacy reader fields, and stale reserved v2 fields require an additive raw-JSON transformation
a write commits and loses its response, requiring the exact same operation ID on retry so one logical success causes exactly one physical rewrite
a failed page checkpoint forces a page replay in which previously rewritten events must be recognized as v2 rather than physically rewritten again
coexisting writers separately update a v1 payload and publish a v2 payload between listing and rewrite, requiring reload, recomputation, and non-overwrite behavior
always-transient and always-conflicting stores distinguish the initial attempt from each configured retry and verify partial counters plus errors.Is identity
checkpoint probes return commit-then-error with either the attempted target or a foreign durable state, requiring exact outcome reconciliation
